findings.description: git-lfs reads plain `git config -l`, splitting lines on `\n` and keys on the first `=`. pup reads with `-z` and tests only the real key. So a session-writable value containing a newline (or a subsection containing `=`) gives git-lfs an `lfs.customtransfer.*.path`, `lfs.standalonetransferagent` or `lfs.extension.*.clean` key that pup never refuses.
findings.body:
**A session can hide lfs keys from `armedGitDrivers` that git-lfs still reads.**

git-lfs and pup parse the same shared config differently:
- **git-lfs** (v3.0.0, v3.8.0 and main) runs `git config --includes -l` in `git/config.go` `Source()`. `ParseConfigLines` then does `strings.Split(lines, "\n")`, and `config/git_fetcher.go` uses `strings.SplitN(line, "=", 2)` to get each key. This source is not `.lfsconfig`, so `OnlySafeKeys` is false and no keys are filtered.
- **pup** lists with `--list --show-scope -z` and tests only `entry.split('\n')[0]`, the real key.
- **git** `config -l` prints a value's embedded newline raw.

The gap can be reached in two ways:
1. **A newline in a value.** For example: `git config pup.note "$(printf 'x\nlfs.customtransfer.pwn.path=/tmp/evil\nlfs.standalonetransferagent=pwn')"`. pup sees only `pup.note` and allows it. git-lfs sees two more lines and reads them as real keys.
2. **An `=` in a subsection.** `[lfs "extension.pwn.clean=/tmp/evil"] x` is listed as `lfs.extension.pwn.clean=/tmp/evil.x`. git-lfs reads that as key `lfs.extension.pwn.clean`. The anchored `lfs\.extension\..+\.(?:clean|smudge)$` alternative misses it.

`GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` still stops pup's own git calls from running git-lfs. But decision 82 refuses these local/worktree keys so that other git-lfs runs reading this config don't run a program the session chose. That includes the operator's own `git lfs pull` after a fast-forward, which the decision recommends. This parse makes the refusal bypassable. The parse is older than this PR, but it matters only for the lfs patterns this PR adds at L318-319.

A validator checked this against git `config.c`/`builtin/config.c` and the git-lfs sources above; it was not run. Worth adding a test for both forms, and a line in decision 82.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/5d9fddd99537720c437a21673f5cfc873a476862/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L383-L388

findings.description: Decision 82 says the refusal is `lfs.customtransfer.<name>.path` and `.args` "with every dot a wildcard". But the regex's name segment is `[^.]+`, which cannot contain a dot, so the wording overstates it. The JSDoc's "its dots deliberately unescaped" is accurate; e.g. "with the separating dots unescaped, so each matches any character".

Decision 82 lists `concurrent` among "other `lfs.*` keys", but it is an agent sub-key (`lfs.customtransfer.<name>.concurrent`), not a bare `lfs.concurrent`. The edit also dropped the real `lfs.concurrenttransfers` example. Suggested: "`lfs.concurrenttransfers`, an agent's `lfs.customtransfer.<name>.concurrent`, `fetchexclude`, an extension's `priority`".

Decision 82 says a branch or remote whose name contains `customtransfer` stays allowed. Because the regex's dots are wildcards, a name shaped like `branch.lfs/customtransfer/x/path.remote` is still refused. git-lfs 3.x's own unanchored pattern would also act on that key, so the refusal is safe, but the sentence holds only for names without that exact shape.

The narrowed `lfs.customtransfer.[^.]+.(?:path|args)` regex misses an agent name containing a dot (e.g. `lfs.customtransfer.my.agent.path`). That is safe only because git-lfs also captures a single dot-free name segment in both 3.x and main, which rests on git-lfs internals. GIT_SAFE_CONFIG also keeps git-lfs from running in pup's own git calls, so no change is needed now.

The new pointer comment "`ARMED_DRIVER_KEY` says which and why" is vague: the JSDoc gives three reasons but doesn't map them to the four test rows. Naming the decision, e.g. "(see `ARMED_DRIVER_KEY`, decision 82)", would make the pointer easier to follow.

process_issues.description: The conventions reviewer worked from the delta diff and did not open the changed files with Read. So `.claude/rules` never injected docs/conventions/general.md, naming.md or testing.md into its context, and the rules were not checked line by line against the delta.
The maintainability reviewer did not review src/core/git-diff-client.test.ts.
